hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides change across the period, from strongly basic on the left to strongly acidic on the right.

Remember that $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ dissolves to give $\text{NaOH}$, and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ dissolves to give phosphoric acid, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and do not react with water.
Look for the pair where both oxides actually react, one to make a colourless alkali and the other to make a colourless acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 oxide trend**

Think left to right across Period 3. Basic character decreases and acidic character increases.

$\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ are basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$/$\text{SO}_3$ are acidic.

**Check which oxides react with water**

This is the key filter. Not all oxides dissolve.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$
This gives a colourless alkaline solution.

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$
This gives a colourless acidic solution.

In contrast, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble and does not react with water. $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent solid and does not react with water either.

**Match to the description**

We need both oxides to react, one alkaline and one acidic, both colourless.

Only the $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ (alkaline) plus $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ (acidic) pair fits perfectly.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble and shows no reaction with water, and $\text{SiO}_2$ is also insoluble and unreactive with water. Neither forms a solution, so this trap tests forgetting solubility.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ does react to give acidic $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, but $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ does not react with water at all. Students choosing this remember the acidic oxide but forget $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble.
options.C: Correct. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ reacts to form colourless $\text{NaOH}$ solution which is strongly alkaline, and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ reacts to form colourless $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ solution which is strongly acidic. Both conditions are met.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ correctly gives an alkaline solution, but $\text{SiO}_2$ does not react with water to give an acid, even though it is classed as an acidic oxide. It simply remains as an insoluble solid.
